title: Tuna & Cabbage Crunch Wraps
description: Creamy tuna and crisp cabbage make a quick inexpensive wrap with more crunch than a standard tuna sandwich.
substitutions: Use plain Greek yogurt for some or all of the mayonnaise.
Use shredded lettuce instead of cabbage if that is what you have.

cookSteps.text: Mix 1 drained can tuna with 3 tablespoons mayonnaise, 1 teaspoon mustard, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper.
Fold in 1 cup thinly sliced cabbage. Divide between 2 large tortillas, roll tightly, and serve.

storage: Refrigerate filling up to 2 days. For best texture, assemble wraps just before eating.

title: One-Pot Tomato Lentil Rice
description: Rice and lentils simmer with tomatoes in one pot for a simple pantry dinner with very little hands-on work.
substitutions: Stir in a handful of spinach during the final 5 minutes if available.

steps.text: Simmer until the rice and lentils are tender.

cookSteps.text: Combine 3/4 cup rice, 1/2 cup lentils, 1 can diced tomatoes, 2 1/2 cups broth or water, 1 teaspoon garlic powder, 1 teaspoon Italian seasoning, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper in a medium saucepan.
Bring to a boil, cover, reduce to low, and simmer 25–30 minutes until the lentils and rice are tender. Check near the end and add a splash of water if needed.
Remove from the heat and let stand covered for 5 minutes before fluffing.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days or freeze up to 2 months. Reheat with a splash of water.

title: Broccoli Cheddar Baked Potatoes
description: Fluffy baked potatoes filled with broccoli and melted cheddar for an easy meatless comfort meal.
substitutions: Use frozen broccoli and cook it until just tender.
Use any good melting cheese instead of cheddar.

steps.text: Fill with butter, broccoli, and cheese.

cookSteps.text: Heat the oven to 425°F. Pierce 2 large russet potatoes with a fork and bake 45–50 minutes until very tender.
During the final 8 minutes, steam or microwave 2 cups broccoli florets until tender.
Split the potatoes. Add 1 tablespoon butter to each, season with 1/4 teaspoon salt and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper divided between them, then top with broccoli and 1 cup shredded cheddar.
Return to the oven for 3–5 minutes until the cheese melts.

storage: Refrigerate assembled leftovers up to 3 days. Reheat until hot throughout.

title: Apple Peanut Butter Toast Roll-Ups
description: Flattened bread rolled around peanut butter and diced apple, then toasted in a skillet for a quick sweet breakfast or snack.
substitutions: Use mashed banana instead of apple.
Use sunflower seed butter if peanut butter is not suitable.

cookSteps.text: Flatten 4 bread slices with a rolling pin or sturdy cup. Spread each with 1 tablespoon peanut butter.
Divide 1/2 cup finely diced apple among the slices, sprinkle with 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon, and roll each slice tightly.
Melt 1 teaspoon butter in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the roll-ups seam-side down first, turning until golden on all sides, about 6–8 minutes.

storage: Best fresh. Refrigerate leftovers up to 2 days and reheat briefly in a skillet.
